{{Quote|The Jedi Academy on Dantooine is nothing more than a crater that echoes with the ghosts of dead Jedi. And the Jedi Temple on Coruscant lies empty. The waters in the Room of a Thousand Fountains have fallen still, in reverence to the fallen Jedi... and those now lost.|[[Kreia]] on the destruction of the [[Jedi Enclave]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] abandoning the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the [[First Jedi Purge]]|<ref name="KOTORII">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
The '''Room of a Thousand Fountains''' was a large greenhouse located in the [[First Knowledge Quarter/Legends|First Knowledge Quarter]] at the base of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="SWCL" /> Containing waterfalls and huge amounts of flora, meditative areas, pottery, and stone walkways, the chamber served as a meditative retreat for the members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] while staying in the Temple.<ref name="JATRF" /> Though it was destroyed in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="ROTS" /> the chamber was rebuilt in the [[new Jedi Temple]] circa [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]].<ref name="LOTFBL" />

==History==
{{Quote|Troubled you are, if the garden you seek.|Yoda to Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Jedi Apprentice: The Uncertain Path">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Uncertain Path]]''</ref>}}
Having lost the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], the Jedi Order relocated to the city planet Coruscant where the [[Four Masters/Legends|Four Masters]] had begun to build a Temple that would expand, be destroyed and then rebuilt over the millennia. In all its incarnations it remained largely the same, serving the Order as a retreat from the cityscape of Coruscant and a place to be close to nature.<ref name="SWCL" />

While the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] stayed neutral during the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the Order could not help but defend themselves during the [[Jedi Civil War]]. With many casualties, the Jedi could not hold the Temple as the [[Sith Triumvirate]] began the [[First Jedi Purge|Jedi Purge]] of [[3954 BBY]]. With many of the members of the Order in hiding, the fountains all fell silent in reverence to the fallen and hunted Jedi.<ref name="KOTORII" /> Though reoccupied shortly after the Purge's end, the Temple would fall three centuries later to the resurgent [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] during the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]. The Fountain Room was most likely destroyed during the bombing of the complex.<ref name="Timeline 1" />

Eventually having been rebuilt, the Fountain Room remained in use during the [[Great Peace of the Republic]]. In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], the Room of a Thousand Fountains was the location of several incidents. Unbeknownst to the Jedi, former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Xanatos]], now dubbed a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]], had infiltrated the Temple. Having committed a series of [[Incident at the Jedi Temple|robberies]] at the Temple with the help of Padawan [[Bruck Chun]], Xanatos began to escalate his attacks. In the early morning, as [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] was crossing a bridge in the room, Xanatos detonated a bomb meant to kill the ancient Master. Surviving the attack, Yoda informed the High Council and the Temple went on high alert.<ref name="JATCT">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Captive Temple]]''</ref>

While the Jedi were attempting to discover the intruder, Padawan Chun kidnapped fellow student [[Bant Eerin/Legends|Bant Eerin]], and chained her to the floor of the waterfall pool. Having discovered Chun's treachery, Padawan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] located Eerin and rescued her from drowning. Revealing himself, Chun attacked Kenobi and forced him to the top of the waterfall. While defending himself, Kenobi managed to throw Chun off balance, sending the fallen Padawan over the edge to plummet to his death. While Xanatos fled, the debacle in the Temple ended with only one casualty.<ref name="JATCT" />

Over the next few decades, the Fountain Room was host to many a discussion by the High Council. During the tragedy that was the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Master Yoda met here with [[Maks Leem]] to discuss how the Order had strayed from its path, reflecting on the beauty of the room and how the Temple should have been built on a jungle planet.<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>

During the final days of the Clone Wars, the High Council discovered that the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] they had been hunting was in fact [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. [[Showdown on Coruscant|Moving to arrest him]] a group of Masters led by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] left the Temple, leaving Master [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] and [[Gatemaster]] [[Jurokk]] in charge of the Temple's defenses. While preparing for a potential fight, [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]] took a group of Padawans to the room and began running trough [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] exercises. With Windu having failed to kill the Sith, [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]] was issued to the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. Led by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] marched into the Temple and began to slaughter all the Jedi there. As troopers poured into the Room of a Thousand Fountains, Drallig and his students, ranging from ages four to seventeen, began to deflect their shots. As hard as Drallig and the older students tried, they could not block all the shots and the younger students began to fall. Instructing the students to flee, Drallig and his loyal students charged the line of troopers and were able to push them back. Their victory was short lived as Darth Vader entered the fight and quickly slew Padawans [[Whie Malreaux/Legends|Whie Malreaux]] and [[Bene/Legends|Bene]]. As more and more Knights and Padawans fell, Drallig entered into a duel with Vader, fighting until a lightsaber strike to the shoulder defeated him.<ref name="EPIIIVG">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref>

[[File:CinDrallig.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]] duels [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in the Room of a Thousand Fountains during [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]].]]

In the day following the Temple's capture by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Masters Yoda and Kenobi [[Infiltration of the Jedi Temple/Legends|broke in]] and began searching for answers. Making their way to the Room of a Thousand Fountains, the two crept through the burnt shrubbery and foggy air to find Drallig and his apprentices slain on the stone and dirt floor. In the distance, clone troopers were also sifting through the dead, recording the names of the dead,<ref name="ROTSN">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> and then burning their bodies on the steps of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Temple's public entrance]].<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Into the Unknown">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Into the Unknown]]''</ref> Over the next few months, [[Ferus Olin]] would also break into the Temple in search of a rumored [[Storage floor|Jedi prison]]. While fleeing pursuing troopers, Olin ran through the Fountain room, noting the dried river beds amongst the dead plants. Leaping around the inactive waterfall and through fetid water, Olin escaped the chamber through the ruined ceiling's catwalk system.<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Underworld">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>

While the Temple managed to largely survive the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], even at one point being lightly reoccupied,<ref name="BRS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref> the complex was completely ruined during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref> It would be several years until the [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] of the newly founded [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] would order the rebuilding of the Temple. Erected by the [[Reconstruction Authority]], the Room of a Thousand Fountains was rebuilt in accordance to a specific request by Grand Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the founder of the [[new Jedi Order]]. This request came after having seen mention of the room in documents found in the recovered [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]].<ref name="Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref> The [[New Jedi Temple|new Temple]] would eventually be finished and re-inhabited, the Fountain Room once again housing exotic planets and flowing waters.<ref name="LOTFBL" />

In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], the Fountain room would play host to the disguised [[Lumiya]], Dark Lady of the Sith. Led into the Temple by Knight [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], the Sith was able to convince Solo of her level-headedness and her ability to train him to become a Sith himself without letting her hate of the Jedi get the better of her. Earlier that same year, Solo had [[Flow-walking|flow-walked]] back in time to the Fountain room as it had stood in the old Temple. Through the eye of time Solo witnessed his grandfather, Darth Vader, slay Drallig and his students. Through this, he saw the faulty thinking of Vader and pledged to be a better Sith Lord.<ref name="LOTFBL" />

As the Jedi were blamed for failure to prevent the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Interim Grand Master [[Kenth Hamner]] met with Knight [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] in this chamber. Organa Solo had become increasingly disobedient following the exile of her brother, Grand Master Skywalker, and required a reprimand by Hamner.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Omen">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref>

==Layout==
Located at the base of the Jedi Temple's [[First Knowledge Quarter/Legends|northwestern side]], this seven story tall green house was one of the Temple's major focal points.<ref name="SWCL" /> The main entrance to the chamber consisted a short passage behind huge wooden doors, emptying onto a platform from which several stone and dirt paths diverged. The winding paths cut through potted plants and large displays of exotic foliage from across the galaxy. Little bridges crossed streams that flowed from unseen sources. Benches lined the paths, encouraging meditation and reflection. Fountains could be heard trickling from anywhere in the chamber, along with the roar of the waterfall at the room's center. Some fountains were concealed by the shrubbery, but others were brilliantly displayed in the center of stone walkways.<ref name="JATRF" />

Along with its uses for meditation some Jedi came here for lightsaber practice; the Jedi Councils sometimes met in the chamber due to its peacefulness and serenity.<ref name="JATCT" /> The room served not only as a place of beauty, but also a display room for the tokens of thanks and appreciation given to the Temple by planetary governments over the history of the Republic. Gifts in the form of foreign flora were often sent to the Order and placed in the chamber. Among the collection was a stand of [[hylaian marsh bamboo]],<ref name="ROTSN" /> [[assari]] trees, and a [[Bhansgrek/Legends|bhansgrek]] bush grove.<ref name="LOTFBL" />

Beside the beauty of the gardens, the chamber also was home to a technological wonder. In the rafters of the room was a large collection of lighting banks that disguised the ceiling as an outdoor sky. The combination of light and canvas completed the illusion that gave the room its feel of a completely separate environment from that of Coruscant. Beyond the canvas was a system of catwalks and ramps which allowed the [[Temple employee]]s and servicemen to move about unseen amongst the lighting and atmospheric control banks.<ref name="JATRF" /> After Operation: Knightfall, the fabric was left hanging in tatters, with the catwalks broken free and hanging precariously down into the open area above the destroyed waterfalls.<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Underworld">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>
